purpose: Prove additivity of the maximal simple-branched-cover ordinary-rank lower bound, derive connected-sum MRC cases from the retained families, and exhibit a rigorous nonuniversality boundary at T(4,7).
uniform_theorem: For palettes S_i containing the common moving pair{0,1}, union of size R and |S_i|=r_i, the simple R-cover of the connected sum is the connected sum of the Y_i and beta copies of S1xS2, where beta=sum(r_i-2)-(R-2). Knot normal generation forces every restricted monodromy to have exactly one nontrivial orbit, so this describes every simple cover of a connected sum. Grushko rank additivity then gives C(K#L)=C(K)+C(L)-1 for C(K)=max(r-1+rank pi1Y_phi).
boundary: C<=mr, and C(T(4,7))=3 while mr=bridge4. No assertion that this additive invariant solves full MRC, or that meridional rank is additive for all knots. Prior conditional Coxeter additivity credited. General free-product rank is an explicit classical input, not inferred from finite controls.
verification: Construct literal connected-sum PDs and transposition assignments, check the lifted sphere-component graph, and compute exact folded branched-cover homology. Independent arc tracing, reverse-word matrix reconstruction and unimodular Smith-step replay must match. A separate Reidemeister-Schreier word calculation and binary matrix witness check the T47 boundary. Corrupt palette, missing free factor, false Smith step and torus witness must reject.
scope: Uniform written topology/normal-generation/rank arguments plus finite input controls. No all-knot MRC solution, global novelty, specialist/formal verification, numerical recognition or new293-panel sweep. Source read and external theorem import depths explicit.
